# Integration Guides

### Claude Code

Add to `.mcp.json` (auto-generated by `cgh init`):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cgh": {
      "command": "cgh",
      "args": ["serve", "--root", ".", "--watch", "--reindex"],
      "env": {
        "CODEGRAPH_AUTH_KEY": "<auto-generated key from .codegraph/auth.key>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

See `integrations/claude-code.md` for hooks setup and best practices.

**Across a `/clear` or a compaction.** The `SessionEnd` and `PreCompact`
hooks that `cgh init` installs read the session transcript and record an
automatic digest: the last requests, the files edited, the commands run and
the end of the last answer. No model call is involved, so this works even when
nobody checkpointed. After a `/clear`, the `SessionStart` header shows a short
recap of that previous session, and the model can continue it through the
`resume` tool or ignore it. For the decisions behind the work, run
`/cgh-checkpoint` before clearing: the skill has the model write the goal,
what is done, the decisions, what is open and the next step.

**What cgh adds to every session.** cgh writes one file Claude Code loads at
session start, `.claude/rules/cgh-usage.md` (about 2.3 KB; older versions
wrote 6 to 10 KB, and before the rules directory a block inside `CLAUDE.md`).
`cgh doctor` shows it as `stale` when the copy is an older, longer text, or
when the rule and a leftover `CLAUDE.md` block are both there; `cgh setup
claude` rewrites it. The hooks add a header of a few hundred bytes at
session start, a one-line compaction hint per size threshold, and a full
hint on the first Grep or shell search for code (a one-line reminder after
that, in the same session).

The rest of what a session carries is the repo's own. Measured on ondonne
and wedbridge lots, a ticket session starts with 25 to 48 KB of `CLAUDE.md`,
rules and memory, then loads path-scoped rules (a `paths:` frontmatter, in
`~/.claude/rules/` or the repo's `.claude/rules/`) the first time it touches
a matching file: 1 to 33 KB more per session. Each one rides on every later
request. To trim it, keep a path-scoped rule to the few lines an edit must
not miss and move the rest into a skill, which loads only when invoked; keep
the root `CLAUDE.md` to what every task needs. Nested `CLAUDE.md` files also
load on demand: `terraform init` copies a module repo's `CLAUDE.md` into each
`.terraform/modules/<name>/`, so do not read module sources there; read the
module repo itself.

### Cursor

Add to `.cursor/mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cgh": {
      "command": "cgh",
      "args": ["serve", "--root", ".", "--watch", "--reindex"],
      "env": {
        "CODEGRAPH_AUTH_KEY": "<auto-generated key from .codegraph/auth.key>"

  }
}
```

### IBM Bob

`cgh setup bob` registers the MCP server in `.bob/mcp.json`, installs
the bundled skills under `.bob/skills/` (Bob speaks the same Agent
Skills standard as Claude Code), and drops the usage guidelines in
`.bob/rules/`.

Bob compacts a task around 190k tokens and caps it at 270k, without telling
the model, and its hooks cannot make the model write anything at the end of
a task. `cgh setup bob` (and `cgh init --tools bob`) therefore also writes
session hooks into `.bob/settings.json`, next to any hooks already there:

| Event | What cgh does |
|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | gives the model its session id and the resume header |
| `PostToolUse` | journals the files the agent writes and the commands it runs |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | asks for a checkpoint after `checkpoint_every` tool calls without one |
| `Stop`, `PreCompact` | turns the journal into an automatic session digest |
| `PreToolUse` | only with `checkpoint_gate` set: blocks one tool call until the model checkpoints |

The automatic digest records what changed, not why; the model's own
`checkpoint` carries the decisions. `PreCompact` is documented for Bob
Shell; an IDE without the event ignores it. Tune both thresholds in the
`[bob]` table of the cgh config.

### Supervising the owner (Spero, Monit, cron)

The owner of a repo lives only while an agent needs it: it starts on the
first MCP call and exits when the last agent disconnects. A supervisor must
therefore never keep it alive. The one thing worth watching is an owner that
is still running but no longer answers (a stuck process, a poisoned graph
connection), because every agent call then fails until someone runs
`cgh stop`.

`cgh doctor --owner` is the probe for that. It exits 0 when no owner runs,
when the owner answers, when it is busy indexing or still starting (its
first two minutes), and 1 only when the owner is alive and silent. A repo
directory that was deleted counts as no owner, so a stale target does no
harm. It never starts an owner.

With [Spero](https://github.com/altikva/spero), one target per indexed repo:

```yaml
version: 1
frozen: false

targets:
  - name: cgh-owner-myrepo
    provider: local
    probe:
      type: command
      params:
        command: "cgh doctor --owner --root /path/to/myrepo"
        timeout: 30
      interval: 60
    remediations:
      # Stops the stuck owner and does NOT restart it: the next agent call
      # starts a fresh one, and no agent means no owner.
      - type: respawn
        params:
          start: "cgh stop --root /path/to/myrepo"
        autonomy: auto
        max_attempts: 2
```

`max_attempts: 2` makes `spero watch` act on the second failed probe in a
row, so one slow answer does not stop a healthy owner. A one-shot
`spero run` starts its failure count at zero each time; use `max_attempts: 1`
there. Any other supervisor works the same way: run the probe, and on a
non-zero exit run `cgh stop --root <repo>`.

### Automatic Setup

```bash
cgh init         # interactive: detects tools, installs configs
cgh setup all    # non-interactive: generates all integration files
```
